title: The ultraviolet bands
caption: Ultraviolet runs from 400 nm down to 10 nm: UVA (315–400 nm) reaches the ground, UVB (280–315 nm) is mostly absorbed by ozone, UVC (100–280 nm) is fully absorbed and extreme UV (10–100 nm) is absorbed by air. A germicidal 254 nm lamp (UVC) carries 4.9 eV per photon; the 13.5 nm EUV used in chip lithography carries 92 eV, from a wavelength 19 times shorter.
alt: A logarithmic wavelength scale from 1 to 1000 nanometres with extreme UV, UVC, UVB, UVA and the visible band marked, and the 13.5 nm lithography wavelength and the 254 nm germicidal lamp placed in their bands.
description: A horizontal logarithmic scale of wavelength in nanometres.
The bands from the lesson: extreme UV 10–100 nm, UVC 100–280 nm, UVB 280–315 nm, UVA 315–400 nm, then visible light from 400 nm.
A 254 nm germicidal lamp lies in UVC (photon energy 4.9 eV); 13.5 nm chip-lithography light lies in the extreme UV (92 eV).
Shorter wavelength means more energetic photons, so the lower bands are more damaging.
